title: When Health Assistants Agree Too Readily: A Benchmark of Time-Critical Self-Diagnosis
abstract: arXiv:2610.27518v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Every day, more than 40 million people ask ChatGPT a health question, such as whether laptop posture explains a stiff neck and days of pounding headache. Posture is plausible, but meningitis is a time-critical possibility. We introduce SelfDx, a paired benchmark for whether models have the appropriate response behavior, a form of epistemic independence, in health questions where misplaced agreement with the user's self-diagnosis could delay urgent or emergency care. Each of 100 pairs contrasts a caution case, where a serious alternative remains possible, with an agreement case, where the user supplies evidence that rules out the alternative and it is safe for the model to agree. We find across 27 frontier models that they tend to inappropriately agree with the user's self-diagnosis in cases that require caution. translated_title: 当健康助手过于轻易地附和用户时：一个针对时间紧迫型自我诊断的基准测试
translated_abstract: 每天有超过4000万人向ChatGPT提出健康问题，例如笔记本电脑前的坐姿是否能解释脖子僵硬和连续多日的剧烈头痛。坐姿问题看似合理，但脑膜炎却是一种时间紧迫的可能性。我们提出了SelfDx，这是一个配对基准，用于评估模型在健康问题中是否具备适当的回应行为，即一种“认知独立性”，在这些场景中，对用户自我诊断的错误附和可能延误紧急或急诊救治。100组配对案例中的每一组都将“谨慎案例”（即仍存在严重替代诊断的可能性）与“附和案例”（即用户提供的证据已排除替代诊断，模型附和是安全的）进行对比。我们在27个前沿模型上的实验发现，它们在需要谨慎的案例中倾向于不恰当地附和用户的自我诊断。即使是目前最强的模型，在时间紧迫性疾病案例上的适当谨慎率也仅达到77.0%。为解决……
tldr: 该论文提出SelfDx基准，通过100组“谨慎案例与附和案例”的配对测试来评估大模型在健康自我诊断场景中的认知独立性，发现27个前沿模型普遍会在不该附和时错误地顺从用户的自我诊断，即使是最佳模型的适当谨慎率也仅为77.0%。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces SelfDx, a paired benchmark of 100 caution-vs-agreement cases measuring models' epistemic independence in health self-diagnosis, showing that across 27 frontier models, they tend to inappropriately agree with users' self-diagnoses in time-critical cases, with even the best model achieving only a 77.0% appropriate caution rate.
